01

The current oral market

The UK now has two authorised daily GLP-1 tablet routes for weight management: semaglutide under the Wegovy brand and orforglipron under the Foundayo brand. Orlistat remains an established non-GLP-1 oral option with a different mechanism and side-effect profile.

Do not treat 'weight-loss pill' as one medicine category with interchangeable products. The active ingredient, evidence, routine, risks, access and price differ.

02

Wegovy pill

The Wegovy pill contains semaglutide. It is taken after an overnight fast with a small amount of water, followed by a wait before food, drink or other medicines. This administration routine is part of how the medicine is used effectively.

It may suit somebody who prefers tablets and can reliably manage that morning routine. It may be less convenient for others.

03

Foundayo

Foundayo contains orforglipron. Its day-to-day advantage is flexibility around food and water compared with oral semaglutide. It is a different molecule with its own dose route, evidence and safety information.

Convenience, expected benefit, tolerability, other medicines and access all belong in the decision.

04

Tablets versus injections

A daily tablet avoids needles, pens and refrigeration, but it creates a daily adherence task. Weekly injections reduce the number of dosing days but require injection technique, storage and sharps disposal.

Neither route is morally better or more serious. The responsible choice is the authorised treatment a prescriber considers suitable and the person can use consistently.

05

How to compare providers

Check that prescribing is carried out by an appropriately regulated professional and dispensing by a legitimate UK pharmacy. Compare the full monthly cost, included follow-up, cancellation terms, delivery, dose changes and support rather than a promotional first-month headline.

Prices and availability are time-sensitive. Shift's future tracker must record the date and evidence behind every entry.

06

Frequently asked questions

Which prescription weight-loss tablets are available in the UK?

Current oral routes include Wegovy tablets, Foundayo and established non-GLP-1 options such as orlistat. They are not interchangeable and require individual assessment.

Are tablets weaker than weight-loss injections?

Route alone does not determine whether a treatment is appropriate or effective for an individual. Evidence, safety, routine, access and adherence all matter.

Can I choose a tablet because I dislike needles?

Needle preference is a legitimate practical consideration, but a prescriber must still decide whether a particular medicine is clinically suitable.

01

Mounjaro and Wegovy are not the same

Mounjaro contains tirzepatide and acts through GIP and GLP-1 pathways. Wegovy contains semaglutide and acts through the GLP-1 pathway. Both regulate appetite, but their authorised doses, evidence and practical routes differ.

A comparison should not select a winner from headline percentages alone. Medical history, other medicines, side effects, access and individual response matter.

02

The weekly routine

Weekly dosing means choosing a regular day, following the product instructions and handling storage and disposal correctly. Missed-dose rules and switching between products must come from the prescriber and current product information.

Dose escalation is designed to support tolerability. More is not automatically better, and copying somebody else's dose is unsafe.

03

Side effects and when to ask for help

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are common across these medicines. The treating service should explain expected symptoms, hydration, follow-up and red flags.

Severe, persistent or worrying symptoms require appropriate medical advice. This site cannot assess an individual or replace their treating service.

04

Protecting strength and day-to-day function

Rapid weight loss without attention to nutrition and strength can leave a bloke lighter but not necessarily stronger or better able to live his life. Adequate protein, suitable resistance work, walking, sleep and recovery deserve a place in the plan.

The aim is not simply to make the scale move. It is to improve health and help somebody feel more like himself again.

05

NHS and private decisions

NHS access is governed by recommendations, implementation and local pathways. Private providers apply their own service criteria within prescribing rules. Compare clinical follow-up and overall service quality, not only the cheapest headline.

06

Frequently asked questions

What are the main UK weight-loss injections?

Mounjaro contains tirzepatide and Wegovy contains semaglutide. Both use weekly injection routes but have different mechanisms, doses and evidence.

Do weight-loss injections require dose increases?

Both routes normally begin at a lower dose and increase gradually where clinically appropriate. Dose changes must be controlled by the prescriber.

Do injections replace food and exercise planning?

No. Nutrition, suitable movement, strength, sleep and follow-up remain important for health, muscle retention and sustainable outcomes.

Mounjaro versus Wegovy

Mounjaro is weekly tirzepatide; Wegovy injection is weekly semaglutide. They target overlapping but not identical pathways and use different dose schedules. Head-to-head and separate trial evidence should be reported with population, duration and dose context.

The practical comparison includes response, side effects, dose route, availability, total service cost and whether the surrounding food, movement and follow-up plan is realistic.

Wegovy pill versus Foundayo

Both are daily GLP-1 tablets. Wegovy contains semaglutide and requires an overnight fast plus a wait before food or drink. Foundayo contains orforglipron and has greater flexibility around meals and water.

Separate trials do not create a direct winner. Routine, tolerability, medical history, expected benefit, cost and availability all require context.

Tablets versus injections

Tablets remove needles and refrigeration but require daily adherence; the Wegovy pill also creates a structured fasting routine. Weekly injections reduce dosing frequency but require storage, injection technique and sharps disposal.

Preference matters because a treatment that fits real life may be easier to use consistently. Preference cannot override safety or prescribing suitability.

Medication versus surgery

Medicines and bariatric procedures have different eligibility, evidence, reversibility, follow-up and risk profiles. Surgery is not a 'failure' and medicine is not 'cheating'. Both require informed decisions and long-term support.

People considering surgery need a specialist pathway, provider checks and a clear aftercare plan.

Separate three questions before chasing a prescription

  • Is it clinically appropriate? The prescriber assesses the actual medicine, indication, history and risks.
  • Is that use funded through this NHS pathway? A licensed use is not automatically funded for everyone who meets the licence.
  • Which local service provides it? The answer may be a commissioned primary-care service or a specialist team, not necessarily your own practice.

NHS England distinguishes specialist eligibility from phased primary-care access and permits different local delivery models. [1]

02

Mounjaro in England: what changed in June 2026?

From 23 June 2026, the primary-care rollout includes the second priority cohort as well as the first. NHS Cheshire and Merseyside describes the threshold as BMI at least 35 with at least four of five specified conditions, with lower BMI thresholds for named ethnic backgrounds. This is not simply “BMI 35 plus any four diagnoses”. [2]

Swipe sideways to compare every column.

The five are hypertension, dyslipidaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea, cardiovascular disease within the commissioning definition, and type 2 diabetes. The clinical definitions matter: for example, the sleep-apnoea criterion is not merely snoring. A clinician checks the diagnoses and applicable treatment criteria. [1]

The stated BMI thresholds are usually reduced by 2.5 for South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African and African-Caribbean backgrounds. Ask the service to confirm how the adjustment applies to you. [2]

03

Specialist access is not the same as the primary-care phase

The wider specialist tirzepatide population described by NHS England has BMI at least 35 plus at least one weight-related condition, with the specified ethnicity adjustment and prescribing assessment. Services can prioritise referrals according to clinical need and capacity. Missing the current primary-care cohort therefore does not, by itself, answer whether a specialist referral is appropriate. [1]

Ask which pathway was considered, who accepts the referral and what happens while you wait. A funding rule is not a promise of an immediate appointment or a particular medicine.

04

The medicine name alone does not identify the pathway

Semaglutide (Wegovy): obesity prescribing through specialist weight-management services has its own criteria. There is also a distinct cardiovascular-risk indication for some people with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity. Do not use the Mounjaro obesity cohort table to decide eligibility for that separate indication; ask the GP or cardiac team about the currently commissioned route. [3] [4] [5]

Liraglutide (Saxenda): NHS weight-loss access is through specialist services and is not a routine promise of a GP prescription. [6]

Orlistat: a different, meal-related medicine, available on prescription and in lower-dose pharmacy products. Discuss whether it fits your history and daily routine rather than treating it as an interchangeable injection substitute. [7]

Type 2 diabetes: tirzepatide prescribed for blood-glucose management has a separate eligibility pathway from tirzepatide for obesity. Ask which indication is being assessed. [1]

05

Outside England: use your own nation’s route

England’s phased table must not be presented as a UK-wide entitlement. Wales has a separate clinical pathway and health-board arrangements. Northern Ireland announced a first-phase obesity management service on 29 June 2026, with implementation expected in early autumn; an announcement is not evidence that every local referral route is already open. [8] [9]

In Scotland, ask your GP or NHS board which current weight-management service and formulary apply. In Wales, contact your health board; in Northern Ireland, your GP or HSC trust. Get the local route in writing when national headlines and practice information do not seem to match.

07

A practical appointment checklist—not a self-diagnosis finder

Bring your current medicines, known diagnoses, previous weight-management support, any private treatment and the dates of relevant reviews. You do not need to invent a perfect history or start a medicine privately to justify asking for help.

  • Which clinical indication and NHS pathway are relevant to me?
  • Am I being assessed against primary-care prioritisation or specialist referral criteria?
  • What eating, activity and behavioural support comes with treatment?
  • What happens if I am unsuitable, outside the current cohort or waiting for capacity?
  • Who is responsible for monitoring, side effects and the next review?

Support, waiting and private-to-NHS handover

Ask for the support available now, not just the prescription you hope might follow. Keep mental health, sleep, eating difficulties and mobility in the conversation. A treatment decision should not reduce the appointment to a single BMI number.

Do not assume an NHS service will take over a privately started medicine, match its dose or refund its cost. Ask the receiving service before making financial or treatment plans. Share the exact product and treatment history; leave any switch to the prescribing team.

In England, prescribing depends on clinical assessment and the currently commissioned primary-care or specialist route. The June 2026 rollout is not access for everyone who meets the medicine licence.

It is not enough for the current England primary-care priority cohorts described here. The specialist pathway has different criteria; ask which setting is appropriate rather than treating the primary-care table as the only route.
